scope: Test fixture only: one integration-test file; no production implementation, system profile, sandbox policy, filtering or timeout change.
platforms: The existing Unix-only fixture uses the wrapper only when shell_name == bash. Linux and macOS Bash fixture instances remain eligible; zsh uses its original /bin/zsh path and arguments. PermissionsExt import is widened from target_os=linux to unix solely because this Unix fixture now creates an executable script.
path_lifetime: The executable is under the existing owned temporary HOME. Its PathBuf remains alive throughout the fixture. Both argv[0] and ShellInfo.path are derived from exactly the same path. The quoted "$@" preserves every argument and exec keeps the process/exit boundary; the wrapper does not read or filter output.

eligibility_proof.reason: Only the requested program path changes. The original sandbox transform retains the command suffix. ShellSnapshotCache runs before the kernel interprets the script shebang. No guard is bypassed or relaxed.

capture_proof.script_behavior: snapshot_state_and_environment_script retains bash_snapshot_script initial explicit source of the controlled HOME/.bashrc when BASH_ENV is empty. The fixture includes only HOME/PATH and has no BASH_ENV override. --noprofile omits host login profiles but does not change this explicit source.
capture_proof.native_capture_behavior: capture_snapshot clones the prepared command, replaces only its script argument, clears env and supplies the original prepared env. Original failure exit, backoff and retry budget stay unchanged. Successful restoration still changes -lc to the existing --norc/-pc invocation, forwarded unmodified by the wrapper.

original_assertions_retained: fallback output exactly (original, empty stderr, Some(0), true)
after repair output exactly recovered or original according to original retry budget
final captures exactly xx or xxx
all original test-case annotations, including pipe/TTY/local/remote and macOS zsh cases
regression_guard: If the wrapper made capture ineligible, the existing captures file read/count and recovered-output assertions would fail. They remain byte-identical.

verification.next: Independent source review followed by native original affected-package/full gates.
